**Revised 10/12 (Old Mercy's rule made plain on the page; no roll, choice, box value or slot changed):** the bell is silent unless the House keeps someone, so the Prior's holding it in Ch 1 was the ordinary silence and the ringing at the gate was the claim. Ch 1 Sc 3: Pell gives the rule at the hearth and the Prior asks how often the law has lapsed once rung; Darrow: "You'd leave your own gate without its law." Sc 4: no law on the gate till she rings; "It starts with the first ringing." Climax: not rung for anyone in years. Ch 2 epigraph counts Wren's time. From here every dawn and dusk must ring while Marrant waits (b1.5's hinge).

**10/11 close (ch02:s1, *Good Night, Captain*, colour mild):** b1.2's night of the gate on the page. Thread 12: the names brought back to the cots by Hollis; Benedek not read, believes it mercy ("It's mercy after all"); why he was not on the list is still on no page; Darrow kept from him his own reading of Marrant's far-cots line against the law of names (no will, no refusal): dread planted for the dawn, no truth spent. Thread 13: Hollis four days dry, his hand shaking under the blanket at the night bell, face to the wall (nobody but Darrow saw). Thread 16: c01.5c fired: a grey cloak at the bars sent the Captain of the Ninth the Confessor's good night by his rank, through the gate-ward (the one who drew the wicket's bar); Darrow: "Then tell him you gave it." The camp sits up in turns round one fire, four sitting, one walking the terrace edge, nobody lying down, the censer in one man's hand; the winch-house one lamp. Maelis: "Held"; one moment more and nothing left to tie it to; still soft at the thaw. Rank beat paid (Kindled; `rank_on_page`). His throat shut on the oath's first word (thread 12/Benedek's oath: lips only, again). Last words between them: "Good night, Captain." / "Good night, Ser Benedek." (b1.2 at dawn lands on this.)

**10/12, ch02:between-3 (*Same Paper*):** after the night bell Darrow walked the hall to the three Ninth men from the gate (unnamed; near the banked fire on the far side: the oldest, forearm splinted, rode with the Ninth longer than Darrow commanded it; one head bound; one asleep) and offered to disown them to Marrant. They refused: "Same paper"; "We came up the Steps on other men's backs, Captain. We'll not go down them on yours." Callback **c02.3a** (`later`): fire where Marrant's terms or the kneeling come back to him in front of his own (Book V's `old_banner`, where the nineteen come one by one, stays its own payoff). Thread 13: Hollis awake to the wall, "All three?", "Ninth", hand still shaking; his knucklebones on the stool between the cots. **Continuity for slot 2:** Darrow's walk down the hall and back was early in the night, before he slept; "nobody passed" covers the hours after. Benedek is not on the page in this Between.

**10/12, ch02:between-4 (*Him Who Can Stand*):** knucklebones for a story told true (the game's second time; Finesse 11 on the nose). Thread 13: Hollis's hands steady while they hold something and shake when they don't (on the page now, twice); he chanted "the bones go to him who can stand" and heard it. His confession: at the window he thought it good, for a heartbeat, that the Captain kneel for the rest (callback **c02.4a**, `later`: fire where Hollis must stand by Darrow at a cost, or the kneeling is put to Darrow in his hearing; it feeds `r.b4.hollis_lives` in spirit, never by number). Darrow's line, "I had three heartbeats in that river. I know what a man can think in one": the Three Heartbeats named by him to Hollis for the first time, as a measure, not a telling; nothing of Aldric's horse (thread 1 untouched). The chair, the Seated Blade and the Measured Hand stay unspoken: the bones were a game, not a lesson. Two Betweens after ch02:s1 are now written; anything more before slot 2 is two lines. **Continuity for slot 2:** both Betweens fall early in the night; Darrow slept after; Benedek is on the page in neither.

**Revised 10/12 (editorial pass on ch02 Betweens 3 and 4; the roll, the ledger deltas and the slots unchanged):** each Between now changes an obligation. *Same Paper*: the three disagree (the oldest: "You. Deciding"; the second would take Marrant's bargain if there were one and says so; the old one's "backs" line stands), Darrow drops the order and asks, and promises **"You'll be asked"** (c02.3a now carries that promise; sister to Wren's c02.1a). *Him Who Can Stand* opens on the first ("They wouldn't let me go down for them." / "Would you?"); the game is compressed; the confession hurts first ("You wanted me to go." "For a moment." "And now?"), Hollis's now is that he would carry Darrow down the Steps himself before Marrant had him, then the heartbeats line, then the full name and Hollis's oath to say the next such thought aloud (**"Out loud. Bells help me"**; c02.4a carries it: fire where he keeps a thought he swore to say, or stands by Darrow at a cost). The Between rules were changed the same day (`/play` §3, `style.md` §3, `design.md` §9): every Between changes an understanding, a relationship or a small obligation.

Thread 12: Benedek found at the dawn bell of the feast, breathing, eyes open, frost on his lips, no oath; at the word the hall looked to the door, and Darrow kept its eyes on the lad instead. Feast: the bread went down to the gate under the grey cloaks' eyes; whether they took it is on no page (the kitchen's book was never settled). Lore: house.ysolde spoken (a lay brother's "Saint Ysolde's bread"; another's scoff, revised 10/12: "a bone-setter with a bad temper and a bell. Call her saint to her face and you'd have got the bell").

Ione wears the undercroft key on a cord at her neck. Darrow kept the glass's look out of the hall (c02.13a kept). Knot II: no stair down for Darrow on the page until Knot III ties (Tue 10/20).

Maelis keeps the chip and suspects (T1); Darrow believes it looks like a chip off a field-stone and kept it out of the hall before the whole House when asked (02:climax, c02.13a kept); the reader. The hall knows only that the Mender found a black glass and will say what it is when she knows. Not Hollis, not Wren
